Chapter 9: Praying for Faith and Spiritual Growth
You know, faith isn’t really a finish line—it’s more like a journey we’re all on. For so many parents, the deepest hope is that their kids will grow spiritually, that they’ll find peace, a sense of purpose, and a connection to something bigger than themselves. That hope shapes so many prayers, doesn’t it? But let’s be honest—faith can feel fragile, especially when the world keeps questioning, challenging, and sometimes even hurting us.
Picture this: a mother watches her son. He once lit up with belief, eager to take part in everything. But now, he’s drifted away from those habits that used to ground him. She worries. Did she do enough? She replays old conversations, searching for answers. But then, she realizes—faith isn’t something you can force. So, her prayers shift. She starts asking for his curiosity to spark again, for his questions to dig deeper, and for grace to find him—wherever he happens to be on his journey.
Most of us don’t really notice how much faith ebbs and flows. There are seasons of doubt, and you know what? That’s normal. Sometimes, it’s even necessary. Parents often wish for certainty—they want to know their child’s faith is steady. But prayer can become a way to let go, to trust that the story isn’t finished, that every tough question might actually lead to growth, and that wandering doesn’t mean being lost forever.
Think about a father, watching his daughter struggle with disappointment in her faith community. He prays—not for quick fixes, but for healing, for new connections, for her heart to stay open. And in time, she does find a new group. Somewhere that welcomes her, somewhere her questions are respected. He realizes his prayers made space for her to discover her own path, on her own terms.
Spiritual growth rarely moves in a straight line, does it? There are setbacks, new discoveries, moments of doubt and moments of wonder. As parents, you can pray for openness, resilience, and those unexpected encounters with grace. And above all, you can trust that faith—once it’s planted—can survive even the harshest seasons.
